**Finding submitted: COMPLIANT** (no redline proposed).

**Summary for GOVLAW:**

| Element | Document position | Playbook |
|---|---|---|
| Governing law | New York, conflicts disclaimed (§15.5) | **Preferred** ✓ |
| Forum | JAMS arbitration, seat redacted; court carve-outs for IP, interim relief, enforcement | Not walk-away (domestic, not foreign arbitration) |
| Pre-step | JSC → Designated Senior Officers escalation | Permitted ✓ |

The governing law hits the preferred position outright, and the dispute-resolution architecture stays firmly within US/domestic bounds with multiple court carve-outs, so it does not fail the fallback. Per the classification semantics, the election of domestic JAMS arbitration instead of exclusive New York County courts is a sub-element short of preferred wording — noted in the rationale, not redlined.

**One diligence item to close out:** the arbitral seat is redacted (`arbitration in [***] before [***] arbitrators`). I flagged this in the rationale rather than as a deviation because JAMS is a US administrator and every surrounding mechanic points domestic — but if the unredacted seat turns out to be outside the accepted list, this flips to a deviation (mandatory arbitration seated abroad is express walk-away territory) and the minimal fix would be to replace only the seat words in p0629 with "New York, New York."

I also confirmed the Sanofi-favorable items and left them alone: §2.10(b)/p0234 gives *our* Designated Senior Officer final decision-making authority on escalated matters, and §15.6(f)'s punitive damages waiver is mutual.
